thread.title: Broadcom CFO Sees Potential M&A Targets in U.S.

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Broadcom CFO Sees Potential M&A Targets in U.S.
text:
Following a report this afternoon by chip giant Broadcom ( AVGO ), fiscal Q1 revenue and profit that topped analysts' expectations, and a higher revenue forecast for this quarter, CFO Thomas Krause on a conference call with analysts said the fact the company had to walk away this week from its hostile bid for Qualcomm ( QCOM ), "we don't see this week's events putting any constraint on our ability to pursue acquisitions more broadly going forward."
Moreover, Krause added that he and CEO Hock Tan see potential M&A targets:
The allocation of the remaining 50% of free cash flow is governed by the returns that we believe that can drive via acquisitions versus buying AVGO stock and/or paying down debt. As you all know, Hock and I are quite familiar with the industry landscape. And sitting here today, we do see potential targets that are consistent with our proven business model and can also can drive returns well in excess of what we otherwise achieve buying our own stock and paying down debt. If this view changes, rest assured, we will not hesitate to change our approach. Providing superior returns for shareholders has been and always will be our focus.
Krause said Qualcomm is unique and future deals will be done solely with cash :
One final point I want to make, Qualcomm was clearly a unique and very large acquisition opportunity. Given the maturity of the industry, the consolidation it is seeing and our relative size now, our future acquisitions are much more likely to be funded with cash available on on our balance sheet and without the need to flex the balance sheet much beyond our current financial policy of 2x net leverage.
Krause expressed appreciation for Qualcomm and Broadcom shareholders, adding "I have to say we are touched by the ISS report issued just last night that continues to recommend the Broadcom independent nominees."
Krause said that it appears "the 11 Qualcomm nominees" to its board of directors "are only garnering between 15% to 16% of the outstanding shares, not necessarily something to celebrate in San Diego."
Regarding last quarter’s results, Krause said it "was all driven by wireless growth,” and he here alluded to the delayed ramp in production of Apple ’s ( AAPL ) iPhone X :
First quarter 2018 wireless revenue growth was driven by the ramp of the next-generation platform from our last North American smartphone customer. As you may recall, this ramp was pushed out into the first quarter from the fourth quarter as compared to prior years. This push-up coupled with a very large increase in our content in this new platform drove the substantial year-on-year growth in revenue in the first quarter.
However, Krause told analysts to expect a sharper-than-usual drop-off in wireless this quarter:
But as we look into the second quarter of fiscal '18, we expect -- we are expecting a much larger-than-typical seasonal decline in wireless revenue as shipments to our North American smartphone customer will trend down sharply from the first quarter.
He said the drop will be partially offset by ramping production for Samsung Electronics ’s ( 005930KS ) “ Galaxy S9 ,” introduced last month, without mentioning Samsung by name.
Krause said as wireless drops off, the company expects revenue from wireline products, especially for cloud computing data centers, to take center stage this quarter:
[In FYQ2] This wired segment returned with a vengeance. We project strong double-digit sequential revenue growth, and this growth is driven by very strong increase in demand for our networking products from cloud and data centers as well as the weighted seasonal recovery in broadband carrier access. Set-top box continued to be flat.
During the Q&A, Tan told analysts that fiber optics continues to be an area of weakness in the market for wired communications parts:
What we don't see a sharp recovery is, obviously, fiber optics in networking. The old fiber optics out of data centers continue to be better (inaudible) has shown renewed strength. So basically, data center cloud that are showing -- enterprise showing a lot of strength to offset metro networks and, in our case, to continued flatness in set-top box.
Broadcom shares are down $3.28, or 1%, at $264.48, in late trading.
